comment: The capture matrix, in ONE place. .github/workflows/capture.yml reads this
to build its job matrix and scripts/common/check-coverage reads it to say
which cells have a profile, so the plan and the report cannot disagree.
A matrix written into the workflow and a coverage report written from
somewhere else is a value in two places with no check that they agree.
enabled false is a cell that is PLANNED and not attempted. It is reported
as such rather than dropped, because a coverage report that lists only what
was tried cannot show what is missing. TODO/corpus.md, CORPUS-02.
required true means check-coverage --require-rows can be asked to fail on
it. Nothing is required by default: the flag names what a caller cares
about.
os is the runner label and it is the only field the workflow needs that the
corpus does not have. browser, channel and platform are the three keys a
profile's route is derived from, spelled exactly as the corpus spells them.
route says HOW the lane gets the browser, and it is the field DRIVER-08
added. installed takes whatever the runner image has, which is what every
capture so far did and why every published profile carries
captured.acquisition null. vendor purges the machine and installs the
current branded build from the vendor's own channel. for-testing purges and
installs an exact build from the automation index, which is UNBRANDED.
scripts/common/provision-browser.sh is the tool and --route is the flag.
build names the exact build a for-testing cell wants. The automation index
publishes a SUBSET of builds: measured 2026-09-02 it carried 67 builds of
Chrome 151 and neither of the two the runner images served, so a build here
is one the index was checked to have.

cells.why: The cheapest lane there is: the runner image ships Chrome, so this needs no acquisition at all. ⭐ Route changed to vendor on 2026-09-02, which is the ruling applied: the lane purges the machine and installs the current branded build rather than measuring whatever the image shipped. ⚠ Measured in provision.yml run 33628209454: the vendor channel served 152.0.7977.75 on Linux and 152.0.7977.76 on Windows one hour apart, so this route does NOT give both platforms one build.

The one platform the corpus already has, captured again on a runner rather than on a laptop. Two profiles of one build on two platforms is what decides whether the TLS half is platform-independent. ⭐ Route changed to vendor on 2026-09-02, which is the ruling applied: the lane purges the machine and installs the current branded build rather than measuring whatever the image shipped. ⚠ Measured in provision.yml run 33628209454: the vendor channel served 152.0.7977.75 on Linux and 152.0.7977.76 on Windows one hour apart, so this route does NOT give both platforms one build.

The same engine with a different brand list and User-Agent, so it isolates branding from engine at almost no cost. ⭐ Provisioned from the vendor enterprise index as of 2026-09-02 rather than taken from the image: the index publishes a SHA-256 per artefact, so this is the first cell whose acquisition can be checked against the publisher. ⚠ branded stays true: the enterprise index serves the vendor own product, unlike the Chrome automation index. The image Edge could not capture at all, because its SUID sandbox helper was not configured, which capture.yml run 33615327503 recorded and DRIVER-10 fixes.

The unbranded build of the version the corpus already holds from a laptop, so one build across two platforms and two brands becomes comparable. ⭐ Enabled 2026-09-03, by the operator's ruling: Channel::ForTesting landed, so the row publishes at its own route and no branded build shares a path with it. ⚠ NOTHING HAS EXERCISED THIS LANE'S CAPTURE PATH. capture.yml allows every lane to fail alone, so the first attempt reports rather than breaking the run, and DRIVER-06 owns the difference the lane exists to measure.

The other half of the pair above, and the one that measures whether the TLS half is platform-independent at a build both platforms genuinely run. ⭐ Enabled 2026-09-03 with it, and for the same reason. ⚠ Its capture path is equally unexercised.

A third platform and a second architecture. Waiting on DRIVER-05 having a route that serves a macOS build, and on the identity writer taking its platform from the run rather than from a two-way branch. The automation index spells this platform mac-arm64 and the corpus spells it macos-arm64, so a for-testing cell here translates deliberately.
How the project gets ahead of a release rather than behind it. Waiting on acquisition: no runner image ships a beta channel, and provision-browser's vendor route serves the stable channel only.

A genuinely different TLS stack and the highest-value non-Chrome lane. ⭐ The resolver knows the family as of 2026-09-04, which is what this cell used to be waiting on: b_ids_driver::Family has a firefox variant, candidates on both platforms, and Source::ApplicationIni, which is the only source that answers for a Firefox layout. Measured on one Windows host, it resolves 148.0.2 from application.ini. ⛔ Still not enabled, and the blocker has MOVED rather than gone: b_ids_driver::drive passes Chromium switches and nothing else, so it refuses a non-Chromium family rather than launching one with arguments it misreads. A launch path for Gecko is what this cell now waits on.

The control that proves which fields are branding and which are engine: whatever differs from the chrome cell beside it is branding. ⛔ THE PLAN DID NOT LIST THIS CELL AT ALL until 2026-09-04, while CORPUS-02's acceptance names chromium as a required row, so the plan and the acceptance disagreed about what was even planned. ⚠ Waiting on acquisition rather than on the resolver, which knows the family now: there is no vendor channel serving a Chromium build addressable by the version a profile records, and the runner image serves it as a snap, which is a different install mechanism and a different sandbox. DRIVER-10 says this cell may end as a recorded refusal rather than a lane.
